parts.problem_md:
Write these numbers in order of size.

`2 over 3 space space space space space space space space space space 7 over 11 space space space space space space space space space 60 percent sign space space space space space space space space 5 over 8 space space space space space space space space 0.613`

Start with the smallest number.
parts.solution_md:
> *Convert the numbers so that they are all in the same form*

> *Converting to fractions, decimals or percentages will all give the same final result but converting to decimals is most efficient using a calculator*

> *Convert *$\frac{2}{3},\frac{7}{11}\mathrm{and}\frac{5}{8}$* to decimals using the fraction button on the calculator or using division*

`table row cell 2 divided by 3 end cell equals cell 0.666... end cell row cell 7 divided by 11 end cell equals cell 0.636... end cell row cell 5 divided by 8 end cell equals cell 0.625 end cell end table`

> *Convert 60% to a decimal by dividing by 100*

$60\div100=0.6$

> *0.613 is already in decimal form*

> *Write the decimals as a list, making sure that the place value columns align*

> *It is helpful to use zeros as place holders so that each number contains the same number of digits*

$0.666...\,0.636...\,0.625\,0.600\,0.613$

> *Starting with the ones column and working to the right, look down the place value columns comparing the size of digits and selecting the smallest value in turn*

> *The numbers in correct ascending order are:*

$0.600\,0.613\,0.625\,0.636...\,0.666...$

> *Write them out in ascending order using the original form given in the question*

**Final answer:** **60%, 0.613, **$\frac{5}{8},\frac{7}{11},\frac{2}{3}$

**[B1 B1 B1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **B1**: At least 3 numbers in the correct order.
> 
> **B1**: At least 3 numbers in the correct order. Or for the three fractions converted to decimals or percentages correctly.
> 
> **B1**: Correct order.

parts.problem_md:
(i) Work out the value of $\frac{\sqrt{2.9\times3.76}}{4.2-0.63}$

Write down all the figures on your calculator display

(ii) Give your answer to part (d) (i) correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.solution_md:
(i)

> **[exam-tip]**
> You can type the whole expression into your calculator. Or you can type  the numerator and denominator separately. As it is worth more than one mark, it is a good idea to type them in separately. This means if you type one number in incorrectly, you still might get one of the marks.

> *Calculate the numerator using a calculator*

$\sqrt{2.9\times3.76}=3.302...$

**[M1]**

> *Divide this value by the denominator, using the answer button on the calculator to ensure accuracy*

`3.302... divided by open parentheses 4.2 minus 0.63 close parentheses equals 0.9249637341...`

**Final answer:** **0.924963741**

**[A1]**

(ii)

> *3 significant figures means the first 3 digits starting from the first non-zero digit*

> *The fourth non-zero digit must be checked to decide whether to round up or down*

*0.924**<u>9</u>**63741*

> *9 is more than 5 so the third significant figure will round up*

**Final answer:** **0.925**

**[B1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> The mark is awarded if an incorrect answer to part (i) has been rounded correctly to 4 significant figures.
